standard.title: Questioning, Predicting and Hypothesising
standard.description: develop investigable questions, reasoned predictions and hypotheses to test relationships and develop explanatory models
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can pose investigable relationship questions and make reasoned predictions justified with scientific knowledge (AC9S7I01, 7-8 band). They now extend to formulating testable hypotheses — predictions framed as if-then statements that can be explicitly supported or refuted by evidence.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop investigable questions, formulate testable hypotheses (if-then statements with explicit causal reasoning), and pose questions that explore explanatory models — distinguishing hypothesis from prediction by the causal mechanism specified.

nodes.label: Hypotheses specify testable causal relationships
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can formulate a scientific hypothesis as a testable if-then statement specifying a causal relationship, and explain what evidence would support or refute it.
nodes.minimum_width: Students write one testable hypothesis for a given scenario in if-then format and identify the evidence that would support or refute it.
nodes.typical_width: Students formulate hypotheses for Y9 science contexts (body systems, energy efficiency, carbon cycle, chemical reactions); explain why a hypothesis must be testable by evidence; distinguish hypothesis from prediction by the causal mechanism specified; and develop questions that explore explanatory models rather than just describe phenomena.
wider: Discuss what makes a hypothesis scientific — why it must be able to be supported or refuted — and examine historical cases where hypotheses were untestable and therefore unscientific
Develop investigable questions to explore explanatory models: 'How is sound wave transfer affected by medium density? What causes body temperature to rise during illness?'
Examine how a hypothesis about body systems (temperature regulation, blood glucose) maps to the negative feedback model — connecting hypothesis formulation to model testing
nodes.hinge_reason: Hypothesis formulation is the entry point for all Y9 investigation planning (AC9S9I02). Students who cannot write a testable if-then statement cannot design a valid investigation — the variable identification, validity criteria, and evaluation of conclusions in subsequent nodes all depend on the hypothesis providing a clear causal claim to test.

response_modes.reason: Students conflate prediction with hypothesis, writing 'I think X will happen' rather than specifying the causal mechanism as an if-then statement. Making the structure explicit — if [independent variable changes], then [dependent variable will change] because [causal mechanism] — and distinguishing it from prediction by the presence of the mechanism, is the scaffold that produces genuine hypothesis formulation.

success_criteria: Writes a hypothesis in testable if-then format specifying a causal relationship
Identifies what evidence would support and what evidence would refute the hypothesis
